A1.justification: Both PDFs present the same Q-chunking research work. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching content across relocations and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original offline-to-online reinforcement-learning experiments on 25 OGBench tasks and three robomimic tasks, including learning curves, ablations, trajectory analyses, and runtime measurements.

after.justification: v3 retains original experimental results and adds comparison methods, QC-IFQL results, and expanded chunk-length analyses in Section 5 and Appendix E.

M1.justification: Section 4.3 adds QC-IFQL as another instantiation of Q-chunking using IFQL. The original QC and QC-FQL policy construction, training losses, and update procedures remain unchanged; Algorithms 1–2 are relocated to Appendix C.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same five OGBench domains comprising 25 tasks and the robomimic lift, can, and square tasks, with the same play-style and multi-human datasets. Added ablations use cube-triple and cube-quadruple tasks already evaluated in v1.

E2.justification: v3 adds evaluated OGBench comparisons with IQL, ReBRAC, IFQL, IFQL-n, and SUPE-GT, a ground-truth-reward adaptation of a skill-based method (Tables 1 and 6). QC-RLPD also enters the puzzle and scene comparisons, whereas v1 reports its cube-task results only. This substantially broadens the comparison methods.

E3.justification: The chunk-length sweep adds h=15 and h=50, and a new cube-quadruple-task4 experiment compares QC-FQL and FQL-n at matched lengths 3, 5, 7, and 9 (v3 Figures 6, 14–15). Existing training budgets, 50-episode evaluations, and default training settings are retained.

E4.justification: v3 substantially extends tests of chunking's benefits and boundaries: longer-chunk and individual-task analyses reveal failure conditions, while Figure 15 tests learning stability against matched n-step backups across several lengths. Tables 1 and 6 additionally isolate chunking's benefit for IFQL. The earlier trajectory, Gaussian-policy, critic-ensemble, and UTD analyses remain.

E5.justification: The default four OGBench seeds, five robomimic seeds, 95% confidence intervals, and 5000 stratified samples remain unchanged. v3's checklist item 7 additionally identifies interval estimation as bootstrapping, a limited reporting clarification that does not establish additional runs or a changed estimator.

E6.justification: v3 adds substantial results for previously unevaluated methods: Tables 1 and 6 report overall online success of 59% for QC-IFQL, 47% for IFQL, 44% for IFQL-n, and 52% for SUPE-GT. Added sensitivity results show long-chunk failures and n-step learning collapse. Existing robomimic, Gaussian-policy, ensemble/UTD, and runtime results are retained.

T1.justification: v1 gives an informal unbiased-backup argument in Section 4.1. v3 adds Proposition A.1 and an accompanying proof with explicit trajectory and value-estimation assumptions, constituting a substantial formal addition. However, its estimate and proof omit the terminal gamma^n discount factor required by the discounted formulation in Equation 7.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the central claims about behavior-constrained action chunking, temporally coherent exploration, unbiased multistep backups, and strong offline-to-online performance. The main QC/QC-FQL contribution framing is unchanged.

C2.justification: v1 broadly says larger chunks help. v3's Section 5.5 qualifies this with nonmonotonic performance and proposes reduced policy reactivity or harder sequence prediction as explanations for excessive chunk lengths. Section 6's existing fixed-chunk and high-frequency-feedback limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v3 adds SUPE-GT implementation details and new baselines' tuning settings, per-run and aggregate compute estimates, and parameter counts (Appendices C–D; Table 7). The main-result reproduction estimate is 10,350 GPU hours. Existing QC/QC-FQL implementation details, the RTX-A5000 timing benchmark, and the code pointer were already provided in v1.

R1.justification: Section 2 substantially revises positioning against closely related work. It adds TOP-ERL's related chunked-critic formulation, expands the already-cited Seo and Abbeel work into a detailed comparison of chunked critics, behavior cloning, and factorization, and discusses earlier macro-action methods. These changes clarify substantive overlap and distinctions.

P1.justification: Language revisions are concentrated in related work, comparator descriptions, implementation explanations, and sensitivity discussion. Algorithms 1–2 move to Appendix C, and a NeurIPS checklist and new appendix sections are inserted. The abstract, introduction, core method exposition, conclusion, and main narrative sequence are largely retained.

P2.justification: Results presentation is substantially reorganized through new aggregate and per-task OGBench Tables 1 and 6, combined selected-results plots in Appendix Figure 11, expanded Figure 6, new Figures 14–15, and parameter-count Table 7. Existing plots and algorithm boxes are also relocated or resized; many underlying figures are retained.

improvement.justification: v3 strengthens the empirical case through a skill-based comparator, additional offline-RL comparisons, and analyses testing chunk-length failure conditions and n-step instability. Clearer research positioning and compute disclosures improve transparency. These provide a limited net improvement, while the new Proposition A.1's missing terminal discount factor leaves its formal justification inconsistent with Equation 7.
